text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, exactly one of A19, A20 and A21 ran in almost every case — A19 in about 35 in 100 traces, A20 in about 30 and A21 in about 36 — while the three practically never occurred in the same trace, so they behaved as mutually exclusive alternatives. In the later window, each of them appears in only about 1 in 200 traces. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL007, REL008, REL016]

- A26 and A27 were not observed in any of the 200 earlier traces, and A28 in only 1; in the later window, all three occur in every trace, about once per case, at roughly 0.38 of the trace's relative position. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, POS005, POS006, POS007]

- In the later window, A26, A27 and A28 always run together and without a fixed order: each pair co-occurs in 100 in 100 traces, with either order in about half of the cases (for example, A26 before A27 in 50 in 100 and A27 before A26 in 49 in 100). Before, these pairs were never or almost never seen together. [REL031, REL032, REL037]

- The new block sits between A44 and A29: A44 precedes each of A26, A27 and A28 in all but about 1 in 200 later traces, and each of the three precedes A29 in about 99 in 100; the step distance from A44 to A29 grew from mostly 2–3 steps to mostly 4–5 steps, and A28 now reaches A29 within 1–3 steps (the single earlier observation had it immediately before A29). Earlier, A44 preceded each of A19/A20/A21 and each of them preceded A29, each relation in roughly 30–36 in 100 traces, consistent with one alternative sitting between the two anchors. [REL012, REL013, REL020, REL021, REL027, REL028, REL033, REL034, REL042, REL043, LAG003, LAG005]

- A10 became rarer: about 26 in 100 traces before, about 11 in 100 later. In the later window, A10 occurs only together with A26/A27/A28 (its co-occurrence with them equals its full participation), whereas before it usually appeared without A19/A20/A21. [OCC001, REL001, REL004, REL005, REL006]

- Downstream adjustments: A29's mean relative position moved from about 0.40 to about 0.44; A45 still occurs in every trace but is now typically preceded by A26 (about 64 in 100, with about 36 interleaved), where earlier A19 sometimes preceded it; A46 now appears in about 58 in 100 traces (about 69 before) and usually together with A26 preceding it. [POS008, REL014, REL015, REL035, REL036]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in the segment between A44 and A29: the mutually exclusive activities A19, A20 and A21, of which exactly one was executed per case in the earlier window, are no longer observed (about 1 in 200 traces each), and A26, A27 and A28, previously unobserved, now run in every case — together, in no fixed order among themselves, placed after A44 and before A29. The participation reversal (0 of 200 vs 200 of 200 traces) is far beyond sampling variation; the relational evidence directly shows the before-alternatives and after-always-together behaviour; order and step-distance evidence shows the placement directly; and the screening flagged 65 control-flow items where fewer than 1 would be expected without a change, so the ensemble is not what a stable process produces. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL007, REL031, REL033, REL034, REL042, REL043, LAG003, LAG005]

The main limitation is that the evidence contains no direct transition observations, so the exact neighbours of the new block are inferred from order and step distance rather than observed edges, and unobserved activities could sit between A44 and the block or between the block and A29. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A26/A27/A28 are renamed successors of A19/A20/A21 rather than net-new work; even then, the shift from "exactly one of three" to "all three, unordered" would remain a real behavioural change. Several relational items also reuse the same traces, so they corroborate rather than independently confirm one another. [OCC005, REL031, LAG005]

Other differences: A10's participation fell from about 26 to about 11 in 100 traces, and in the few later traces where it appears (about 7 in 200) it sits one step after A44 alongside the new trio, though this rests on few observations; A46's participation slipped from about 69 to about 58 in 100 traces. [OCC001, LAG004, REL036]
